1.2: O venerable goddess, hear my pray'r, for labour pains are thy peculiar care;
1.3: In thee, when stretch'd upon the bed of grief, the sex as in a mirror view relief.
1.4: Guard of the race, endued with gentle mind, to helpless youth, benevolent and kind;
1.5: Benignant nourisher; great Nature's key belongs to no divinity but thee.
1.6: Thou dwell'st with all immanifest to sight, and solemn festivals are thy delight.
1.7: Thine is the talk to loose the virgin's zone, and thou in ev'ry work art seen and known.
1.8: With births you sympathize, tho' pleas'd to see the numerous offspring of fertility;
1.9: When rack'd with nature's pangs and sore distress'd, the sex invoke thee, as the soul's sure rest;
1.10: For thou alone can'st give relief to pain, which art attempts to ease, but tries in vain;
1.11: Assisting goddess [Eileithyia], venerable pow'r, who bring'st relief in labour's dreadful hour;
1.12: Hear, blessed Dian [Artemis], and accept my pray'r, and make the infant race thy constant care.

2.2: Night [Nyx], parent goddess, source of sweet repose, from whom at first both Gods and men arose,
2.3: Hear, blessed Venus [Kypris], deck'd with starry light, in sleep's deep silence dwelling Ebon night!
2.4: Dreams and soft case attend thy dusky train, pleas'd with the length'ned gloom and feaftful strain.
2.5: Dissolving anxious care, the friend of Mirth, with darkling coursers riding round the earth.
2.6: Goddess of phantoms and of shadowy play, whose drowsy pow'r divides the nat'ral day:
2.7: By Fate's decree you constant send the light to deepest hell, remote from mortal sight
2.8: For dire Necessity which nought withstands, invests the world with adamantine bands.
2.9: Be present, Goddess, to thy suppliant's pray'r, desir'd by all, whom all alike revere,
2.10: Blessed, benevolent, with friendly aid dispell the fears of Twilight's dreadful shade.

3.2: Great Heav'n [Ouranos], whose mighty frame no respite knows, father of all, from whom the world arose:
3.3: Hear, bounteous parent, source and end of all, forever whirling round this earthly ball;
3.4: Abode of Gods, whose guardian pow'r surrounds th' eternal World with ever during bounds;
3.5: Whose ample bosom and encircling folds the dire necessity of nature holds.
3.6: Ætherial, earthly, whose all-various frame azure and full of forms, no power can tame.
3.7: All-seeing Heav'n, progenitor of Time [Kronos], forever blessed, deity sublime,
3.8: Propitious on a novel mystic shine, and crown his wishes with a life divine.

4.2: O Ever untam'd Fire [Aither], who reign'st on high in Jove's [Zeus'] dominions ruler of the sky;
4.3: The glorious sun with dazzling lustre bright, and moon and stars from thee derive their light;
4.4: All taming pow'r, ætherial shining fire, whose vivid blasts the heat of life inspire:
4.5: The world's best element, light-bearing pow'r, with starry radiance shining, splendid flow'r,
4.6: O hear my suppliant pray'r, and may thy frame be ever innocent, serene, and tame.

5.2: O Mighty first-begotten [Protogonos], hear my pray'r, two-fold, egg-born, and wand'ring thro' the air,
5.3: Bull-roarer, glorying in thy golden wings, from whom the race of Gods and mortals springs.
5.4: Ericapæus [Erikapaios], celebrated pow'r, ineffable, occult, all shining flow'r.
5.5: From eyes obscure thou wip'st the gloom of night, all-spreading splendour, pure and holy light
5.6: Hence Phanes call'd, the glory of the sky, on waving pinions thro' the world you fly.
5.7: Priapus, dark-ey'd splendour, thee I sing, genial, all-prudent, ever-blessed king,
5.8: With joyful aspect on our rights divine and holy sacrifice propitious shine.

6.2: With holy voice I call the stars [Astron] on high, pure sacred lights and genii of the sky.
6.3: Celestial stars, the progeny of Night [Nyx], in whirling circles beaming far your light,
6.4: Refulgent rays around the heav'ns ye throw, eternal fires, the source of all below.
6.5: With flames significant of Fate ye shine, and aptly rule for men a path divine.
6.6: In seven bright zones ye run with wand'ring flames, and heaven and earth compose your lucid frames:
6.7: With course unwearied, pure and fiery bright forever shining thro' the veil of Night.
6.8: Hail twinkling, joyful, ever wakeful fires! Propitious shine on all my just desires;
6.9: These sacred rites regard with conscious rays, and end our works devoted to your praise.

7.1: The Fumigation from Frankinsence and Manna.
7.2: Hear golden Titan, whose eternal eye with broad survey, illumines all the sky.
7.3: Self-born, unwearied in diffusing light, and to all eyes the mirrour of delight:
7.4: Lord of the seasons, with thy fiery car and leaping coursers, beaming light from far:
7.5: With thy right hand the source of morning light, and with thy left the father of the night.
7.6: Agile and vig'rous, venerable Sun, fiery and bright around the heav'ns you run.
7.7: Foe to the wicked, but the good man's guide, o'er all his steps propitious you preside:
7.8: With various founding, golden lyre, 'tis mine to fill the world with harmony divine.
7.9: Father of ages, guide of prosp'rous deeds, the world's commander, borne by lucid steeds,
7.10: Immortal Jove [Zeus], all-searching, bearing light, source of existence, pure and fiery bright
7.11: Bearer of fruit, almighty lord of years, agil and warm, whom ev'ry pow'r reveres.
7.12: Great eye of Nature and the starry skies, doom'd with immortal flames to set and rise
7.13: Dispensing justice, lover of the stream, the world's great despot, and o'er all supreme.
7.14: Faithful defender, and the eye of right, of steeds the ruler, and of life the light:
7.15: With founding whip four fiery steeds you guide, when in the car of day you glorious ride.
7.16: Propitious on these mystic labours shine, and bless thy suppliants with a life divine.

8.2: Hear, Goddess queen, diffusing silver light, bull-horn'd and wand'ring thro' the gloom of Night.
8.3: With stars surrounded, and with circuit wide Night's torch extending, thro' the heav'ns you ride:
8.4: Female and Male with borrow'd rays you shine, and now full-orb'd, now tending to decline.
8.5: Mother of ages, fruit-producing Moon [Mene], whose amber orb makes Night's reflected noon:
8.6: Lover of horses, splendid, queen of Night, all-seeing pow'r bedeck'd with starry light.
8.7: Lover of vigilance, the foe of strife, in peace rejoicing, and a prudent life:
8.8: Fair lamp of Night, its ornament and friend, who giv'st to Nature's works their destin'd end.
8.9: Queen of the stars, all-wife Diana hail! Deck'd with a graceful robe and shining veil;
8.10: Come, blessed Goddess, prudent, starry, bright, come moony-lamp with chaste and splendid light,
8.11: Shine on these sacred rites with prosp'rous rays, and pleas'd accept thy suppliant's mystic praise.

9.2: Nature [Phusis], all parent, ancient, and divine, O Much-mechanic mother, art is thine;
9.3: Heav'nly, abundant, venerable queen, in ev'ry part of thy dominions seen.
9.4: Untam'd, all-taming, ever splendid light, all ruling, honor'd, and supremly bright.
9.5: Immortal, first-born [Protogeneia], ever still the same, nocturnal, starry, shining, glorious dame.
9.6: Thy feet's still traces in a circling course, by thee are turn'd, with unremitting force.
9.7: Pure ornament of all the pow'rs divine, finite and infinite alike you shine;
9.8: To all things common and in all things known, yet incommunicable and alone.
9.9: Without a father of thy wond'rous frame, thyself the father whence thy essence came.
9.10: All-flourishing, connecting, mingling soul, leader and ruler of this mighty whole.
9.11: Life-bearer, all-sustaining, various nam'd, and for commanding grace and beauty fam'd.
9.12: Justice, supreme in might, whose general sway the waters of the restless deep obey.
9.13: Ætherial, earthly, for the pious glad, sweet to the good, but bitter to the bad.
9.14: All-wife, all bounteous, provident, divine, a rich increase of nutriment is thine;
9.15: Father of all, great nurse, and mother kind, abundant, blessed, all-spermatic mind:
9.16: Mature, impetuous, from whose fertile seeds and plastic hand, this changing scene proceeds.
9.17: All-parent pow'r, to mortal eyes unseen, eternal, moving, all-sagacious queen.
9.18: By thee the world, whose parts in rapid flow, like swift descending streams, no respite know,
9.19: On an eternal hinge, with steady course is whirl'd, with matchless, unremitting force.
9.20: Thron'd on a circling car, thy mighty hand holds and directs, the reins of wide command.
9.21: Various thy essence, honor'd, and the best, of judgement too, the general end and test.
9.22: Intrepid, fatal, all-subduing dame, life-everlasting, Parca, breathing flame.
9.23: Immortal, Providence, the world is thine, and thou art all things, architect divine.
9.24: O blessed Goddess, hear thy suppliant's pray'r, and make my future life, thy constant care;
9.25: Give plenteous seasons, and sufficient wealth, and crown my days with lasting, peace and health.

10.2: I Call strong Pan, the substance of the whole, etherial, marine, earthly, general soul,
10.3: Immortal fire; for all the world is thine, and all are parts of thee, O pow'r divine.
10.4: Come, blessed Pan, whom rural haunts delight, come, leaping, agile, wand'ring, starry light;
10.5: The Hours and Seasons [Horai], wait thy high command, and round thy throne in graceful order stand.
10.6: Goat-footed, horned, Bacchanalian Pan, fanatic pow'r, from whom the world began,
10.7: Whose various parts by thee inspir'd, combine in endless dance and melody divine.
10.8: In thee a refuge from our fears we find, those fears peculiar to the human kind.
10.9: Thee shepherds, streams of water, goats rejoice, thou lov'st the chace, and Echo's secret voice:
10.10: The sportive nymphs, thy ev'ry step attend, and all thy works fulfill their destin'd end.
10.11: O all-producing pow'r, much-fam'd, divine, the world's great ruler, rich increase is thine.
10.12: All-fertile Pæan, heav'nly splendor pure, in fruits rejoicing, and in caves obscure.
10.13: True serpent-horned Jove [Zeus], whose dreadful rage when rous'd, 'tis hard for mortals to asswage.
10.14: By thee the earth wide-bosom'd deep and long, stands on a basis permanent and strong.
10.15: Th' unwearied waters of the rolling sea, profoundly spreading, yield to thy decree.
10.16: Old Ocean [Okeanos] too reveres thy high command, whose liquid arms begirt the solid land.
10.17: The spacious air, whose nutrimental fire, and vivid blasts, the heat of life inspire
10.18: The lighter frame of fire, whose sparkling eye shines on the summit of the azure sky,
10.19: Submit alike to thee, whole general sway all parts of matter, various form'd obey.
10.20: All nature's change thro' thy protecting care, and all mankind thy lib'ral bounties share:
10.21: For these where'er dispers'd thro' boundless space, still find thy providence support their race.
10.22: Come, Bacchanalian, blessed power draw near, fanatic Pan, thy humble suppliant hear,
10.23: Propitious to these holy rites attend, and grant my life may meet a prosp'rous end;
10.24: Drive panic Fury too, wherever found, from human kind, to earth's remotest bound.

11.2: Hear, pow'rful, Hercules [Herakles] untam'd and strong, to whom vast hands, and mighty works belong,
11.3: Almighty Titan, prudent and benign, of various forms, eternal and divine,
11.4: Father of Time [khronos], the theme of gen'ral praise, ineffable, ador'd in various ways.
11.5: Magnanimous, in divination skill'd and in the athletic labours of the field.
11.6: 'Tis thine strong archer, all things to devour, supreme, all-helping, all-producing pow'r;
11.7: To thee mankind as their deliv'rer pray, whose arm can chase the savage tribes away:
11.8: Uweary'd, earth's best blossom, offspring fair, to whom calm peace, and peaceful works are dear.
11.9: Self-born, with primogenial fires you shine, and various names and strength of heart are thine.
11.10: Thy mighty head supports the morning light, and bears untam'd, the silent gloomy night;
11.11: From east to west endu'd with strength divine, twelve glorious labours to absolve is thine;
11.12: Supremely skill'd, thou reign'st in heav'n's abodes, thyself a God amid'st th' immortal Gods.
11.13: With arms unshaken, infinite, divine, come, blessed pow'r, and to our rites incline;
11.14: The mitigations of disease convey, and drive disasterous maladies away.
11.15: Come, shake the branch with thy almighty arm, dismiss thy darts and noxious fate disarm.

12.2: Etherial father, mighty Titan, hear, great fire of Gods and men, whom all revere:
12.3: Endu'd with various council, pure and strong, to whom perfection and decrease belong.
12.4: Consum'd by thee all forms that hourly die, by thee restor'd, their former place supply;
12.5: The world immense in everlasting chains, strong and ineffable thy pow'r contains
12.6: Father of vast eternity, divine, O mighty Saturn [Kronos], various speech is thine:
12.7: Blossom of earth and of the starry skies, husband of Rhea, and Prometheus wife.
12.8: Obstetric Nature, venerable root, from which the various forms of being shoot;
12.9: No parts peculiar can thy pow'r enclose, diffus'd thro' all, from which the world arose,
12.10: O, best of beings, of a subtle mind, propitious hear to holy pray'rs inclin'd;
12.11: The sacred rites benevolent attend, and grant a blameless life, a blessed end.

13.2: Daughter of great Protogonus, divine, illustrious Rhea, to my pray'r incline,
13.3: Who driv'st thy holy car with speed along, drawn by fierce lions, terrible and strong.
13.4: Mother of Jove [Zeus], whose mighty arm can wield th' avenging bolt, and shake the dreadful shield.
13.5: Drum-beating, frantic, of a splendid mien, brass-sounding, honor'd, Saturn's [Kronos'] blessed queen.
13.6: Thou joy'st in mountains and tumultuous fight, and mankind's horrid howlings, thee delight.
13.7: War's parent, mighty, of majestic frame, deceitful saviour, liberating dame.
13.8: Mother of Gods and men, from whom the earth [Gaia] and lofty heav'ns [Ouranos] derive their glorious birth;
13.9: Th' ætherial gales, the deeply spreading sea goddess ærial form'd, proceed from thee.
13.10: Come, pleas'd with wand'rings, blessed and divine, with peace attended on our labours shine;
13.11: Bring rich abundance, and wherever found drive dire disease, to earth's remotest bound.

14.2: O Jove much-honor'd, Jove [Zeus] supremely great, to thee our holy rites we consecrate,
14.3: Our pray'rs and expiations, king divine, for all things round thy head exalted shine.
14.4: The earth is thine, and mountains swelling high, the sea profound, and all within the sky.
14.5: Saturnian [Kronion] king, descending from above, magnanimous, commanding, sceptred Jove [Zeus];
14.6: All-parent, principle and end of all, whose pow'r almighty, shakes this earthly ball;
14.7: Ev'n Nature trembles at thy mighty nod, loud-sounding, arm'd with light'ning, thund'ring God.
14.8: Source of abundance, purifying king, O various-form'd from whom all natures spring;
14.9: Propitious hear my pray'r, give blameless health, with peace divine, and necessary wealth.

15.2: O Royal Juno [Hera] of majestic mien, aerial-form'd, divine, Jove's [Zeus'] blessed queen,
15.3: Thron'd in the bosom of cærulean air, the race of mortals is thy constant care.
15.4: The cooling gales thy pow'r alone inspires, which nourish life, which ev'ry life desires.
15.5: Mother of clouds and winds, from thee alone producing all things, mortal life is known:
15.6: All natures share thy temp'rament divine, and universal sway alone is thine.
15.7: With founding blasts of wind, the swelling sea and rolling rivers roar, when shook by thee.
15.8: Come, blessed Goddess, fam'd almighty queen, with aspect kind, rejoicing and serene.

16.2: Hear, Neptune [Poseidon], ruler of the sea profound, whose liquid grasp begirts the solid ground;
16.3: Who, at the bottom of the stormy main, dark and deep-bosom'd, hold'st thy wat'ry reign;
16.4: Thy awful hand the brazen trident bears, and ocean's utmost bound, thy will reveres:
16.5: Thee I invoke, whose steeds the foam divide, from whose dark locks the briny waters glide;
16.6: Whose voice loud founding thro' the roaring deep, drives all its billows, in a raging heap;
16.7: When fiercely riding thro' the boiling sea, thy hoarse command the trembling waves obey.
16.8: Earth shaking, dark-hair'd God, the liquid plains (the third division) Fate to thee ordains,
16.9: 'Tis thine, cærulian dæmon, to survey well pleas'd the monsters of the ocean play,
16.10: Confirm earth's basis, and with prosp'rous gales waft ships along, and swell the spacious sails;
16.11: Add gentle Peace, and fair-hair'd Health beside, and pour abundance in a blameless tide.

17.1: Pluto [Plouton], magnanimous, whose realms profound are fix'd beneath the firm and solid ground,
17.2: In the Tartarian plains remote from fight, and wrapt forever in the depths of night;
17.3: Terrestrial Jove [Zeus Khthonios], thy sacred ear incline, and, pleas'd, accept thy mystic's hymn divine.
17.4: Earth's keys to thee, illustrious king belong, its secret gates unlocking, deep and strong.
17.5: 'Tis thine, abundant annual fruits to bear, for needy mortals are thy constant care.
17.6: To thee, great king, Avernus is assign'd, the seat of Gods, and basis of mankind.
17.7: Thy throne is fix'd in Hade's dismal plains, distant, unknown to rest, where darkness reigns;
17.8: Where, destitute of breath, pale spectres dwell, in endless, dire, inexorable hell;
17.9: And in dread Acheron, whose depths obscure, earth's stable roots eternally secure.
17.10: O mighty dæmon, whose decision dread, the future fate determines of the dead,
17.11: With captive Proserpine [Kore], thro' grassy plains, drawn in a four-yok'd car with loosen'd reins,
17.12: Rapt o'er the deep, impell'd by love, you flew 'till Eleusina's city rose to view;
17.13: There, in a wond'rous cave obscure and deep, the sacred maid secure from search you keep,
17.14: The cave of Atthis, whose wide gates display an entrance to the kingdoms void of day.
17.15: Of unapparent works, thou art alone the dispensator, visible and known.
17.16: O pow'r all-ruling, holy, honor'd light, thee sacred poets and their hymns delight:
17.17: Propitious to thy mystic's works incline, rejoicing come, for holy rites are thine.

18.2: O Father Jove [Zeus], who shak'st with fiery light the world deep-sounding from thy lofty height:
18.3: From thee, proceeds th' ætherial lightning's blaze, flashing around intolerable rays.
18.4: Thy sacred thunders shake the blest abodes, the shining regions of th' immortal Gods:
18.5: Thy pow'r divine, the flaming lightning shrouds, with dark investiture, in fluid clouds.
18.6: 'Tis thine to brandish thunders strong and dire, to scatter storms, and dreadful darts of fire;
18.7: With roaring flames involving all around, and bolts of thunder of tremendous sound.
18.8: Thy rapid dart can raise the hair upright, and shake the heart of man with wild afright.
18.9: Sudden, unconquer'd, holy, thund'ring God, 'with noise unbounded, flying all abroad;
18.10: With all-devouring force, entire and strong, horrid, untam'd, thou roll'st the flames along.
18.11: Rapid, ætherial bolt, descending fire, the earth all-parent, trembles at thy ire;
18.12: The sea all-shining; and each beast that hears the sound terrific, with dread horror fears:
18.13: When Nature's face is bright with flashing fire, and in the heavens resound thy thunders dire.
18.14: Thy thunders white, the azure garments tear, and burst the veil of all surrounding air.
18.15: O Jove [Zeus], all-blessed, may thy wrath severe, hurl'd in the bosom of the deep appear,
18.16: And on the tops of mountains be reveal'd, for thy strong arm is not from us conceal'd.
18.17: Propitious to these sacred rites incline, and crown my wishes with a life divine:
18.18: Add royal health, and gentle peace beside, with equal reason, for my constant guide.

19.1: The Fumigation from Frankincense and Manna.
19.2: I Call the mighty, holy, splendid light, aerial, dreadful-sounding, fiery-bright;
19.3: Flaming, aerial-light, with angry voice, lightning thro' lucid clouds with horrid noise.
19.4: Untam'd, to whom resentments dire belong, pure, holy pow'r, all-parent, great and strong:
19.5: Come, and benevolent these rites attend, and grant my days a peaceful, blessed end.

20.2: Ærial clouds, thro' heav'n's resplendent plains who wander, parents of prolific rains;
20.3: Who nourish fruits, whose water'y frames are hurl'd, by winds impetuous, round the mighty world;
20.4: All-thund'ring, lion-roaring, flashing fire, in Air's wide bosom, bearing thunders dire
20.5: Impell'd by ev'ry stormy, sounding gale, with rapid course, along the skies ye fail.
20.6: With blowing winds your wat'ry frames I call, on mother Earth with fruitful show'rs to fall.

21.1: The Fumigation from Frankincense and Manna.
21.2: Tethys I call, with eyes cærulean bright, hid in a veil obscure from human sight;
21.3: Great Ocean's empress, wand'ring thro' the deep, and pleas'd with gentle gales, the earth to sweep;
21.4: Whose blessed waves in swift succession go, and lash the rocky shore with endless flow:
21.5: Delighting in the Sea serene to play, in ships exulting and the wat'ry way.
21.6: Mother of Venus [Kypris], and of clouds obscure, great nurse of beasts, and source of fountains pure.
21.7: O venerable Goddess, hear my pray'r, and make benevolent my life thy care;
21.8: Send, blessed queen, to ships a prosp'rous breeze, and waft them safely o'er the stormy seas.

22.2: O Thou, who doff the roots of Ocean [pontos] keep in seats cærulean, dæmon of the deep,
22.3: With fifty nymphs (attending in thy train, fair virgin artists) glorying thro' the main:
22.4: The dark foundation of the rolling sea and Earth's wide bounds, belong much-fam'd to thee;
22.5: Great dæmon, source of all, whose pow'r can make the Earth's [Deo's] unmeasur'd, holy basis shake,
22.6: When blust'ring winds in secret caverns pent, by thee excited, struggle hard for vent:
22.7: Come, blessed Nereus, listen to my pray'r, and cease to shake the earth with wrath severe;
22.8: Send on our sacred rites abundant health, with peace divine and necessary wealth.

23.2: Daughters of Nereus, resident in caves merg'd deep in Ocean, sporting thro' the waves;
23.3: Fanatic fifty nymphs [Nymphai Einalioi], who thro' the main delight to follow in the Triton's train,
23.4: Rejoicing close behind their cars to keep; whose forms half wild, are nourish'd by the deep,
23.5: With other nymphs of different degree leaping and wand'ring thro' the liquid sea:
23.6: Bright, wat'ry dolphins, sonorous and gay, well pleas'd to sport with bachanalian play;
23.7: Nymphs beauteous-ey'd, whom sacrifice delights, send rich abundance on our mystic rites;
23.8: For you at first disclos'd the rites divine, of holy Bacchus [Bakkhos] and of Proserpine [Phersephoneia],
23.9: Of fair Calliope from whom I spring, and of Apollo bright, the Muse's king.

24.2: Proteus I call, whom Fate decrees, to keep the keys which lock the chambers of the deep;
24.3: First-born, by whose illustrious pow'r alone all Nature's principles are clearly shewn:
24.4: Matter to change with various forms is thine, matter unform'd, capacious, and divine.
24.5: All-honor'd, prudent, whose sagacious mind knows all that was, and is, of ev'ry kind,
24.6: With all that shall be in succeeding time; so vast thy wisdom, wond'rous, and sublime:
24.7: For all things Nature first to thee consign'd, and in thy essence omniform confin'd.
24.8: Come, blessed father, to our rites attend, and grant our happy lives a prosp'rous end.

25.1: The Fumigation from every kind of Seed, except Beans and Aromatics.
25.2: O Goddess, Earth, of Gods and men the source, endu'd with fertile, all destroying force;
25.3: All-parent, bounding, whose prolific pow'rs, produce a store of beauteous fruits and flow'rs,
25.4: All-various maid, th' eternal world's strong base immortal, blessed, crown'd with ev'ry grace;
25.5: From whose wide womb, as from an endless root, fruits, many-form'd, mature and grateful shoot.
25.6: Deep bosom'd, blessed, pleas'd with grassy plains, sweet to the smell, and with prolific rains.
25.7: All flow'ry dæmon, centre of the world, around thy orb, the beauteous stars are hurl'd
25.8: With rapid whirl, eternal and divine, whose frames with matchless skill and wisdom shine.
25.9: Come, blessed Goddess, listen to my pray'r, and make increase of fruits thy constant care;
25.10: With fertile Seasons [Horai] in thy train, draw near, and with propitious mind thy suppliant hear.

26.1: The Fumigation from a Variety of Odoriferous Substances.
26.2: Mother of Gods [Meter Theon], great nurse of all, draw near, divinely honor'd, and regard my pray'r:
26.3: Thron'd on a car, by lions drawn along, by bull-destroying lions, swift and strong,
26.4: Thou sway'st the sceptre of the pole divine, and the world's middle seat, much-fam'd, is thine.
26.5: Hence earth is thine, and needy mortals share their constant food, from thy protecting care:
26.6: From thee at first both Gods and men arose; from thee, the sea and ev'ry river flows.
26.7: Vesta [Hestia], and source of good, thy name we find to mortal men rejoicing to be kind;
26.8: For ev'ry good to give, thy soul delights; come, mighty pow'r, propitious to our rites,
26.9: All-taming, blessed, Phrygian saviour, come, Saturn's [Kronos'] great queen, rejoicing in the drum.
26.10: Celestial, ancient, life-supporting maid, fanatic Goddess, give thy suppliant aid;
26.11: With joyful aspect on our incense shine, and, pleas'd, accept the sacrifice divine.

27.2: Hermes, draw near, and to my pray'r incline, angel of Jove [Zeus], and Maia's son divine;
27.3: Studious of contests, ruler of mankind, with heart almighty, and a prudent mind.
27.4: Celestial messenger, of various skill, whose pow'rful arts could watchful Argus kill:
27.5: With winged feet, 'tis thine thro' air to course, O friend of man, and prophet of discourse:
27.6: Great life-supporter, to rejoice is thine, in arts gymnastic, and in fraud divine:
27.7: With pow'r endu'd all language to explain, of care the loos'ner, and the source of gain.
27.8: Whose hand contains of blameless peace the rod, Corucian, blessed, profitable God;
27.9: Of various speech, whose aid in works we find, and in necessities to mortals kind:
27.10: Dire weapon of the tongue, which men revere, be present, Hermes, and thy suppliant hear;
27.11: Assist my works, conclude my life with peace, give graceful speech, and me memory's increase.

28.1: Daughter of Jove [Zeus], almighty and divine, come, blessed queen, and to these rites incline:
28.2: Only-begotten, Pluto's [Plouton's] honor'd wife, O venerable Goddess, source of life:
28.3: 'Tis thine in earth's profundities to dwell, fast by the wide and dismal gates of hell:
28.4: Jove's [Zeus'] holy offspring, of a beauteous mien, fatal [Praxidike], with lovely locks, infernal queen:
28.5: Source of the furies [Eumenides], whose blest frame proceeds from Jove's [Zeus'] ineffable and secret seeds:
28.6: Mother of Bacchus [Eubouleos], Sonorous, divine, and many-form'd, the parent of the vine:
28.7: The dancing Hours [Horai] attend thee, essence bright, all-ruling virgin, bearing heav'nly light:
28.8: Illustrious, horned, of a bounteous mind, alone desir'd by those of mortal kind.
28.9: O, vernal queen, whom grassy plains delight, sweet to the smell, and pleasing to the sight:
28.10: Whose holy form in budding fruits we view, Earth's vig'rous offspring of a various hue:
28.11: Espous'd in Autumn: life and death alone to wretched mortals from thy power is known:
28.12: For thine the task according to thy will, life to produce, and all that lives to kill.
28.13: Hear, blessed Goddess, send a rich increase of various fruits from earth, with lovely Peace;
28.14: Send Health with gentle hand, and crown my life with blest abundance, free from noisy strife;
28.15: Last in extreme old age the prey of Death, dismiss we willing to the realms beneath,
28.16: To thy fair palace, and the blissful plains where happy spirits dwell, and Pluto [Plouton] reigns.

29.2: Bacchus [Dionysos] I call, loud-sounding and divine, fanatic God, a two-fold shape is thine:
29.3: Thy various names and attributes I sing, O, first-born, thrice begotten, Bacchic king:
29.4: Rural, ineffable, two-form'd, obscure, two-horn'd, with ivy crown'd, euion, pure.
29.5: Bull-fac'd, and martial, bearer of the vine, endu'd with counsel prudent [Eubouleos] and divine:
29.6: Triennial, whom the leaves of vines adorn, of Jove [Zeus] and Proserpine [Persephoneia], occultly born.
29.7: Immortal dæmon, hear my suppliant voice, give me in blameless plenty to rejoice;
29.8: And listen gracious to my mystic pray'r, surrounded with thy choir of nurses fair.

30.1: Leaping Curetes, who with dancing feet and circling measures, armed footsteps beat:
30.2: Whose bosom's mad, fanatic transports fire, who move in rythm to the founding lyre:
30.3: Who traces deaf when lightly leaping tread, arm bearers, strong defenders, rulers dread:
30.4: Propitious omens, guards of Proserpine [Persephone] preserving rites, mysterious and divine
30.5: Come, and benevolent my words attend, (in herds rejoicing), and my life defend.

31.1: Only-Begotten, noble race of Jove, blessed and fierce, who joy'st in caves to rove:
31.2: O, warlike Pallas, whose illustrious kind, ineffable and effable we find:
31.3: Magnanimous and fam'd, the rocky height, and groves, and shady mountains thee delight:
31.4: In arms rejoicing, who with Furies dire and wild, the souls of mortals dost inspire.
31.5: Gymnastic virgin of terrific mind, dire Gorgons bane, unmarried, blessed, kind:
31.6: Mother of arts, imperious; understood, rage to the wicked., wisdom to the good:
31.7: Female and male, the arts of war are thine, fanatic, much-form'd dragoness [Drakaina], divine:
31.8: O'er the Phlegrean giants rous'd to ire, thy coursers driving, with destruction dire.
31.9: Sprung from the head of Jove [Tritogeneia], of splendid mien, purger of evils, all-victorious queen.
31.10: Hear me, O Goddess, when to thee I pray, with supplicating voice both night and day,
31.11: And in my latest hour, peace and health, propitious times, and necessary wealth,
31.12: And, ever present, be thy vot'ries aid, O, much implor'd, art's parent, blue eyed maid.

32.2: O Powerful Victory [Nike], by men desir'd, with adverse breasts to dreadful fury fir'd,
32.3: Thee I invoke, whose might alone can quell contending rage, and molestation fell:
32.4: 'Tis thine in battle to confer the crown, the victor's prize, the mark of sweet renown;
32.5: For thou rul'st all things, Victory [Nike] divine! And glorious strife, and joyful shouts are thine.
32.6: Come, mighty Goddess, and thy suppliant bless, with sparkling eye, elated with success;
32.7: May deeds illustrious thy protection claim, and find, led on by thee immortal Fame.

33.2: Blest Pæan, come, propitious to my pray'r, illustrious pow'r, whom Memphian tribes revere,
33.3: Slayer of Tityus, and the God of health, Lycorian Phœbus, fruitful source of wealth .
33.4: Spermatic, golden-lyr'd, the field from thee receives it's constant, rich fertility.
33.5: Titanic, Grunian, Smynthian, thee I sing, Python-destroying, hallow'd, Delphian king:
33.6: Rural, light-bearer, and the Muse's head, noble and lovely, arm'd with arrows dread:
33.7: Far-darting, Bacchian, two-fold, and divine, pow'r far diffused, and course oblique is thine.
33.8: O, Delian king, whose light-producing eye views all within, and all beneath the sky:
33.9: Whose locks are gold, whose oracles are sure, who, omens good reveal'st, and precepts pure:
33.10: Hear me entreating for the human kind, hear, and be present with benignant mind;
33.11: For thou survey'st this boundless æther all, and ev'ry part of this terrestrial ball
33.12: Abundant, blessed; and thy piercing sight, extends beneath the gloomy, silent night;
33.13: Beyond the darkness, starry-ey'd, profound, the stable roots, deep fix'd by thee are found.
33.14: The world's wide bounds, all-flourishing are thine, thyself all the source and end divine:
33.15: 'Tis thine all Nature's music to inspire, with various-sounding, harmonising lyre;
33.16: Now the last string thou tun'ft to sweet accord, divinely warbling now the highest chord;
33.17: Th' immortal golden lyre, now touch'd by thee, responsive yields a Dorian melody.
33.18: All Nature's tribes to thee their diff'rence owe, and changing seasons from thy music flow
33.19: Hence, mix'd by thee in equal parts, advance Summer and Winter in alternate dance;
33.20: This claims the highest, that the lowest string, the Dorian measure tunes the lovely spring .
33.21: Hence by mankind, Pan-royal, two-horn'd nam'd, emitting whistling winds thro' Syrinx fam'd;
33.22: Since to thy care, the figur'd seal's consign'd, which stamps the world with forms of ev'ry kind.
33.23: Hear me, blest pow'r, and in these rites rejoice, and save thy mystics with a suppliant voice.

34.2: Dark veil'd Latona [Leto], much invoked queen, twin-bearing Goddess, of a noble mien;
34.3: Cæantis [Koiantis] great, a mighty mind is thine, offspring prolific, blest of Jove [Zeus] divine:
34.4: Phœbus proceeds from thee, the God of light, and Dian [Artemis] fair, whom winged darts delight;
34.5: She in Ortygia's honor'd regions born, in Delos he, which mountains high adorn.
34.6: Hear me, O Goddess, with propitious mind, and end these holy rites, with aspect kind.

35.2: Hear me, Jove's [Zeus'] daughter, celebrated queen, Bacchian [Bromia] and Titan, of a noble mien:
35.3: In darts rejoicing and on all to shine, torch-bearing Goddess, Dictynna divine;
35.4: O'er births presiding, and thyself a maid, to labour-pangs imparting ready aid:
35.5: Dissolver of the zone and wrinkl'd care, fierce huntress, glorying in the Sylvan war:
35.6: Swift in the course, in dreadful arrows skill'd, wandering by night, rejoicing in the field:
35.7: Of manly form, erect, of bounteous mind, illustrious dæmon, nurse of human kind:
35.8: Immortal, earthly, bane of monsters fell, 'tis thine; blest maid, on woody hills to dwell:
35.9: Foe of the stag, whom woods and dogs delight, in endless youth who flourish fair and bright.
35.10: O, universal queen, august, divine, a various form, Cydonian pow'r, is thine:
35.11: Dread guardian Goddess, with benignant mind auspicious, come to mystic rites inclin'd
35.12: Give earth a store of beauteous fruits to bear, send gentle Peace, and Health with lovely hair,
35.13: And to the mountains drive Disease and Care.

36.2: O Mighty Titans, who from heav'n [Ouranos] and earth [Gaia] derive your noble and illustrious birth,
36.3: Our fathers fires, in Tartarus profound who dwell, deep merg'd beneath the solid ground:
36.4: Fountains and principles, from whom began th' afflicted, miserable, race of man:
36.5: Who not alone in earth's retreats abide, but in the ocean and the air reside;
36.6: Since ev'ry species from your nature flows, which all prolific, nothing barren knows:
36.7: Avert your rage, if from th' infernal seats one of your tribe should visit our retreats.

37.2: Brass-beating Salians, ministers of Mars [Ares], who guard his arms the instruments of wars
37.3: Whose blessed frames, heav'n, earth, and sea compose, and from whose breath all animals arose:
37.4: Who dwell in Samothracia's sacred ground, defending mortals thro' the sea profound.
37.5: Deathless Curetes [Kouretes], by your pow'r alone, initial rites to men at first were shewn:
37.6: Who shake old Ocean thund'ring to the sky, and stubborn oaks with branches waving high.
37.7: 'Tis your's in glittering arms the earth to beat, with lightly-leaping, rapid, sounding feet;
37.8: Then every beast the noise terrific flies, and the loud tumult wanders thro' the skies:
37.9: The dust your feet excites with matchless force, flies to the clouds amidst their whirling course;
37.10: And ev'ry flower of variegated hue, grows in the dancing motion form'd by you.
37.11: Immortal dæmons, to your pow'rs consign'd the talk to nourish, and destroy mankind.
37.12: When rushing furious with loud tumult dire, o'erwhelm'd, they perish in your dreadful ire;
37.13: And live replenish'd with the balmy air, the food of life, committed to your care.
37.14: When shook by you, the seas, with wild uproar, wide-spreading, and profoundly whirling, roar:
37.15: The concave heav'ns, with Echo's voice resound, when leaves with ruffling noise bestrew the ground.
37.16: Curetes, Corybantes, ruling kings, whose praise the land of Samothracia sings:
37.17: From Jove [Zeus] descended; whose immortal breath sustains the soul, and wafts her back from death;
37.18: Aerial-form'd, much-fam'd, in heav'n ye shine two-fold, in heav'n all-lucid and divine:
37.19: Blowing, serene, from whom abundance springs, nurses of seasons, fruit-producing kings.
37.21: The mighty ruler of this earthly ball, for ever flowing, to these rites I call;
37.22: Martial and blest, unseen by mortal sight, preventing fears, and pleas'd with gloomy night:
37.23: Hence, fancy's terrors are by thee allay'd, all-various king, who lov'st the desart shade:
37.24: Each of thy brothers killing, blood is thine, two-fold Curete [Kourete], many-form'd, divine.
37.25: By thee transmuted Ceres' [Deo's] body pure, became a dragon's savage and obscure:
37.26: Avert thy anger, hear me when I pray, and by fix'd fate, drive fancy's fears away.

39.2: O Universal mother, Ceres [Deo] fam'd august, the source of wealth, and various nam'd:
39.3: Great nurse, all-bounteous, blessed and divine, who joy'st in peace, to nourish corn is thine:
39.4: Goddess of seed, of fruits abundant, fair, harvest and threshing, are thy constant care;
39.5: Who dwell'st in Eleusina's seats retir'd, lovely, delightful queen, by all desir'd.
39.6: Nurse of all mortals, whose benignant mind, first ploughing oxen to the yoke confin'd;
39.7: And gave to men, what nature's wants require, with plenteous means of bliss which all desire.
39.8: In verdure flourishing in honor bright, assessor of great Bacchus [Bromios], bearing light:
39.9: Rejoicing in the reapers sickles, kind, whose nature lucid, earthly, pure, we find.
39.10: Prolific, venerable, Nurse divine, thy daughter loving, holy Proserpine [Koure]:
39.11: A car with dragons yok'd, 'tis thine to guide, and orgies singing round thy throne to ride:
39.12: Only-begotten, much-producing queen, all flowers are thine and fruits of lovely green.
39.13: Bright Goddess, come, with Summer's rich increase swelling and pregnant, leading smiling Peace;
39.14: Come, with fair Concord and imperial Health, and join with these a needful store of wealth.

40.2: Ceralian [Antaia] queen, of celebrated name, from whom both men, and Gods immortal came;
40.3: Who widely wand'ring once, oppress'd with grief, in Eleusina's valley found'st relief,
40.4: Discovering Proserpine [Persephone] thy daughter pure in dread Avernus [Aides], dismal and obscure;
40.5: A sacred youth while thro' the world you stray Bacchus [Dysaulos], attending leader of the way;
40.6: The holy marriage of terrestrial Jove [Zeus Khthonios] relating, while oppress'd with grief you rove;
40.7: Come, much invok'd, and to these rites inclin'd, thy mystic suppliant bless, with fav'ring mind.

41.2: Call Thesmophorus, spermatic God [Dionysos], of various names, who bears the leafy rod:
41.3: Mises [Misa], ineffable, pure, sacred queen, two-fold Iacchus, male and female seen:
41.4: Illustr'ous, whether to rejoice is thine in incense offer'd, in the fane divine;
41.5: Or if in Phrygia most thy soul delights, performing with thy mother sacred rites;
41.6: Or if the land of Cyprus is thy care, well pleas'd to dwell with Cytherea [Kythereia] fair;
41.7: Or if exulting in the fertile plains with thy dark mother Isis, where she reigns,
41.8: With nurses pure attended, near the flood of sacred Egypt, thy divine abode:
41.9: Wherever resident, blest pow'r attend, and with benignant mind these labours end.
41.11: Daughters of Jove [Zeus] and Themis, seasons bright,
41.12: Justice [Dike], and blessed Peace [Eirene], and lawful Right [Eunomia],
41.13: Vernal and grassy, vivid, holy pow'rs, whose balmy breath exhales in lovely flow'rs
41.14: All-colour'd seasons, rich increase your care, circling, for ever flourishing and fair:
41.15: Invested with a veil of shining dew, a flow'ry veil delightful to the view:
41.16: Attending Proserpine [Persephone], when back from night,
41.17: the Fates [Moirai] and Graces [Kharites] Lead her up to light;
41.18: When in a band-harmonious they advance, and joyful round her, form the solemn dance:
41.19: With Ceres [Meter] triumphing, and Jove [Zeus] divine; propitious come, and on our incense shine;
41.20: Give earth a blameless store of fruits to bear, and make a novel mystic's life your care.

43.2: Cadmean Goddess, universal queen, thee, Semele I call, of beauteous mien;
43.3: Deep-bosom'd, lovely flowing locks are thine, mother of Bacchus [Dionysos], joyful and divine,
43.4: The mighty offspring, whom love's thunder bright, forc'd immature, and fright'ned into light:
43.5: Born from the deathless counsels, secret, high, of Jove Saturnian [Zeus Kronion], regent of the sky
43.6: Whom Proserpine [Persephone] permits to view the light, and visit mortals from the realms of night:
43.7: Constant attending on the sacred rites, and feast triennial, which thy soul delights;
43.8: When thy son's wond'rous birth mankind relate, and secrets deep, and holy celebrate.
43.9: Now I invoke thee, great Cadmean queen, to bless these rites with countenance serene.

44.1: Come, blessed Dionysius [Dionysos], various nam'd, bull-fac'd,
44.3: Bassarian God, of universal might, whom swords, and blood, and sacred rage delight:
44.4: In heav'n rejoicing, mad, loud-sounding God, furious inspirer, bearer of the rod:
44.5: By Gods rever'd, who dwell'st with human kind, propitious come, with much-rejoicing mind.

45.2: Liknitan Bacchus [Liknitos Dionysos], bearer of the vine, thee I invoke to bless these rites divine:
45.3: Florid and gay, of nymphs the blossom bright, and of fair Venus [Aphrodite], Goddess of delight,
45.4: 'Tis thine mad footsteps with mad nymphs to beat, dancing thro' groves with lightly leaping feet:
45.5: From Jove's [Zeus'] high counsels nurst by Proserpine [Persephoneia],
45.6: and born the dread of all the pow'rs divine:
45.7: Come, blessed pow'r, regard thy suppliant's voice, propitious come, and in these rites rejoice.

46.2: Bacchus Pericionius [Dionysos Perikionios], hear my pray'r,
46.3: who mad'st the house of Cadmus once thy care,
46.4: With matchless force, his pillars twining round, (when burning thunders shook the solid ground,
46.5: In flaming, founding torrents borne along), propt by thy grasp indissolubly strong.
46.6: Come mighty Bacchus to these rites inclin'd, and bless thy suppliants with rejoicing mind.

47.2: Hear me, illustrious father, dæmon fam'd.
47.3: Great Saturn's [Kronos'] offspring, and Sabasius [Zabazios] nam'd;
47.4: Inserting Bacchus, bearer of the vine, and founding God, within thy thigh divine,
47.5: That when mature, the Dionysian God might burst the bands of his conceal'd abode,
47.6: And come to sacred Tmolus, his delight, where Ippa dwells, all beautiful and bright.
47.7: Come blessed Phrygian God, the king of all, and aid thy mystics, when on thee they call.

48.2: Great nurse of Bacchus [Bakkhos], to my pray'r incline, for holy Sabus' secret rites are thine,
48.3: The mystic rites of Bacchus' nightly choirs, compos'd of sacred, loud-resounding fires:
48.4: Hear me, terrestrial mother, mighty queen, whether on Phyrgia's holy mountain seen,
48.5: Or if to dwell in Tmolus thee delights, with holy aspect come, and bless these rites.

49.1: Hear me, Jove's [Zeus'] son, blest Bacchus, God of wine, born of two mothers, honor'd and divine;
49.2: Lysian, Euion Bacchus, various-nam'd, of Gods the offspring secret, holy, fam'd:
49.3: Fertile and nourishing whose liberal care earth's fruits increases, flourishing and fair;
49.4: Sounding, magnanimous, Lenæan pow'r, O various form'd, medic'nal, holy flow'r:
49.5: Mortals in thee, repose from labour find, delightful charm, desir'd by all mankind:
49.6: Fair-hair'd Euion, Bromian, joyful God, Lysian, invested with the leafy rod.
49.7: To these our rites, benignant pow'r incline, when fav'ring men, or when on Gods you shine;
49.8: Be present to thy mystic's suppliant pray'r, rejoicing come, and fruits abundant bear.

50.2: Nymphs, who from Ocean's [Okeanos'] stream derive your birth, who dwell in liquid caverns of the earth
50.3: Nurses of Bacchus [Bakkhos] secret-coursing pow'r, who fruits sustain, and nourish ev'ry flow'r:
50.4: Earthly, rejoicing, who in meadows dwell, and caves and dens, whose depths extend to hell:
50.5: Holy, oblique, who swiftly soar thro' air, fountains and dews, and mazy streams your care:
50.6: Seen and unseen, who joy with wand'rings wide and gentle course, thro' flow'ry vales to glide;
50.7: With Pan exulting on the mountains height, loud-founding, mad, whom rocks and woods delight:
50.8: Nymphs od'rous, rob'd in white, whose streams exhale the breeze refreshing, and the balmy gale;
50.9: With goats and pastures pleas'd, and beasts of prey, nurses of fruits, unconscious of decay:
50.10: In cold rejoicing, and to cattle kind, sportive thro' ocean wand'ring unconfin'd:
50.11: Nysian, fanatic Nymphs, whom oaks delight, lovers of Spring, Pæonian virgins bright.
50.12: With Bacchus, and with Ceres [Deo], hear my pray'r. And to mankind abundant favour bear;
50.13: Propitious listen to your suppliants voice, come, and benignant in these rites rejoice;
50.14: Give plenteous Seasons, and sufficient wealth, and pour; in lasting streams, continued Health.

51.2: Bacchus fanatic, much-nam'd, blest, divine, bull-fac'd Lenæan, bearer of the vine;
51.3: From fire descended, raging, Nysian king, from whom initial ceremonies spring:
51.4: Liknitan Bacchus, pure and fiery bright, prudent [Eubouleos], crown-bearer, wandering in the night;
51.5: Pupil of Proserpine, mysterious pow'r, triple, ineffable, Jove's [Zeus'] secret flow'r:
51.6: Ericapæus, first-begotten nam'd, of Gods the father, and the offspring fam'd:
51.7: Bearing a sceptre, leader of the choir, whose dancing feet, fanatic Furies fire,
51.8: When the triennial band thou dost inspire.
51.9: Loud-sounding, Tages, of a fiery light, born of two mothers, Amphietus bright:
51.10: Wand'ring on mountains, cloth'd with skins of deer, Apollo, golden-ray'd, whom all revere.
51.11: God of the grape with leaves of ivy crown'd, Bassarian, lovely, virgin-like, renown'd
51.12: Come blessed pow'r, regard thy mystics voice, propitious come, and in these rites rejoice.

52.1: The Fumigation from every Aromatic except Frankincense.
52.2: Terrestrial Dionysius [Dionysos Khthonios], hear my pray'r, awak'ned rise with nymphs of lovely hair:
52.3: Great Amphietus Bacchus, annual God, who laid asleep in Proserpine's [Persephone's] abode,
52.4: Did'st lull to drowsy and oblivious rest, the rites triennial, and the sacred feast;
52.5: Which rous'd again by thee, in graceful ring, thy nurses round thee mystic anthems sing;
52.6: When briskly dancing with rejoicing pow'rs, thou mov'st in concert with the circling hours.
52.7: Come, blessed, fruitful, horned, and divine, and on these rites with joyful aspect shine;
52.8: Accept the general incense and the pray'r, and make prolific holy fruits thy care.

53.2: Great nurse of Bacchus [Bakkhos], to my pray'r incline, Silenus, honor'd by the pow'rs divine
53.3: And by mankind at the triennial feast illustrious dæmon, reverenc'd as the best:
53.4: Holy, august, the source of lawful rites, rejoicing pow'r, whom vigilance delights
53.5: With Sylvans dancing ever young and fair,
53.6: head of the Bacchic Nymphs [Naiades and Bakkhai], who ivy bear.
53.7: With all thy Satyrs on our incense shine, Dæmons wild form'd, and bless the rites divine;
53.8: Come, rouse to sacred Joy thy pupil kin, and Brumal Nymphs with rites Lenæan bring;
53.9: Our orgies shining thro' the night inspire, and bless triumphant pow'r the sacred choir.

54.1: Heav'nly [Ourania], illustrious, laughter-loving queen, sea-born, night-loving, of an awful mien;
54.2: Crafty, from whom necessity [Ananke] first came, producing, nightly, all-connecting dame:
54.3: 'Tis thine the world with harmony to join, for all things spring from thee, O pow'r divine.
54.4: The triple Fates [Moirai] are rul'd by thy decree, and all productions yield alike to thee:
54.5: Whate'er the heav'ns, encircling all contain, earth fruit-producing, and the stormy main,
54.6: Thy sway confesses, and obeys thy nod, awful attendant of the brumal God [Bakkhos]:
54.7: Goddess of marriage, charming to the sight, mother of Loves [Eortes], whom banquetings delight;
54.8: Source of persuasion [Peitho], secret, fav'ring queen, illustrious born, apparent and unseen:
54.9: Spousal, lupercal, and to men inclin'd, prolific, most-desir'd, life-giving., kind:
54.10: Great sceptre-bearer of the Gods, 'tis thine, mortals in necessary bands to join;
54.11: And ev'ry tribe of savage monsters dire in magic chains to bind, thro' mad desire.
54.12: Come, Cyprus-born, and to my pray'r incline, whether exalted in the heav'ns you shine,
54.13: Or pleas'd in Syria's temple to preside, or o'er th' Egyptian plains thy car to guide,
54.14: Fashion'd of gold; and near its sacred flood, fertile and fam'd to fix thy blest abode;
54.15: Or if rejoicing in the azure shores, near where the sea with foaming billows roars,
54.16: The circling choirs of mortals, thy delight, or beauteous nymphs, with eyes cerulean bright,
54.17: Pleas'd by the dusty banks renown'd of old, to drive thy rapid, two-yok'd car of gold;
54.18: Or if in Cyprus with thy mother fair, where married females praise thee ev'ry year,
54.19: And beauteous virgins in the chorus join, Adonis pure to sing and thee divine;
54.20: Come, all-attractive to my pray'r inclin'd, for thee, I call, with holy, reverent mind.

55.2: Much-nam'd, and best of dæmons, hear my pray'r, the desart-loving, deck'd with tender hair;
55.3: Joy to diffuse, by all desir'd is thine, much form'd, Eubulus [Eubouleos]; aliment divine
55.4: Female and Male, all charming to the sight, Adonis ever flourishing and bright;
55.5: At stated periods doom'd to set and rise, with splendid lamp, the glory of the skies.
55.6: Two-horn'd and lovely, reverenc'd with tears, of beauteous form, adorn'd with copious hairs.
55.7: Rejoicing in the chace, all-graceful pow'r, sweet plant of Venus [Aphrodite], Love's [Eors'] delightful
55.8: Descended from the secret bed divine, of lovely-hair'd, infernal Proserpine [Persephone].
55.9: 'Tis thine to fink in Tartarus profound, and shine again thro' heav'ns illustrious round,
55.10: With beauteous temp'ral orb restor'd to sight; come, with earth's fruits, and in these flames delight.

56.2: Hermes I call, whom Fate decrees to dwell in the dire path which leads to deepest hell
56.3: O Bacchic [Bakkheios] Hermes, progeny divine of Dionysius [Dionysos], parent of the vine,
56.4: And of celestial Venus [Aphrodite] Paphian queen, dark eye-lash'd Goddess of a lovely mien:
56.5: Who constant wand'rest thro' the sacred feats
56.6: where hell's dread empress, Proserpine [Persephone], retreats;
56.7: To wretched souls the leader of thc way when Fate decrees, to regions void of day:
56.8: Thine is the wand which causes sleep to fly, or lulls to slumb'rous rest the weary eye;
56.9: For Proserpine [Persephone's] thro' Tart'rus dark and wide gave thee forever flowing souls to guide.
56.10: Come, blessed pow'r the sacrifice attend, and grant our mystic works a happy end.

57.2: I Call great Cupid [Eros], source of sweet delight, holy and pure, and lovely to the sight;
57.3: Darting, and wing'd, impetuous fierce desire, with Gods and mortals playing, wand'ring fire:
57.4: Cautious, and two-fold, keeper of the keys of heav'n and earth, the air, and spreading seas;
57.5: Of all that Ceres' [Deo's] fertile realms contains, by which th' all-parent Goddess life sustains,
57.6: Or dismal Tartarus is doom'd to keep, widely extended, or the sounding, deep;
57.7: For thee, all Nature's various realms obey, who rul'st alone, with universal sway.
57.8: Come, blessed pow'r, regard these mystic fires, and far avert, unlawful mad desires.

58.2: Daughters of darkling Night [Nyx], much-nam'd, draw near infinite Fates [Moirai], and listen to my pray'r;
58.3: Who in the heav'nly lake (where waters white burst from a fountain hid in depths of night,
58.4: And thro' a dark and stony cavern glide, a cave profound, invisible) abide;
58.5: From whence, wide coursing round the boundless earth, your pow'r extends to those of mortal birth
58.6: To men with hope elated, trifling, gay, a race presumptuous, born but to decay;
58.7: Whose life 'tis your's in darkness to conceal to sense impervious, in a purple veil,
58.8: When thro' the fatal plain they joyful ride in one great car, Opinion for their guide;
58.9: 'Till each completes his heav'n-appointed round at Justice, Hope, and Care's concluding bound,
58.10: The terms absolv'd, prescrib'd by ancient law of pow'r immense, and just without a flaw;
58.11: For Fate [Moira] alone with vision unconfin'd, surveys the conduct of the mortal kind.
58.12: Fate is Jove's [Zeus'] perfect and eternal eye, for Jove [Zeus] and Fate [Moira] our ev'ry deed descry.
58.13: Come, gentle pow'rs, well born, benignant, fam'd, Atropos, Lachesis, and Clotho nam'd:
58.14: Unchang'd, aerial, wand'ring in the night, restless, invisible to mortal fight;
58.15: Fates [Moirai] all-producing all-destroying hear, regard the incense and the holy pray'r;
58.16: Propitious listen to these rites inclin'd, and far avert distress with placid mind.

59.2: Hear me, illustrious Graces [Kharites], mighty nam'd, from Jove descended and Eunomia fam'd;
59.3: Thalia, and Aglaia fair and bright, and blest Euphrosyne whom joys delight:
59.4: Mothers of mirth, all lovely to the view, pleasure abundant pure belongs to you:
59.5: Various, forever flourishing and fair, desir'd by mortals, much invok'd in pray'r:
59.6: Circling, dark-ey'd, delightful to mankind, come, and your mystics bless with bounteous mind.

60.1: Thee, Nemesis I call, almighty queen, by whom the deeds of mortal life are seen:
60.2: Eternal, much rever'd, of boundless sight, alone rejoicing in the just and right:
60.3: Changing the counsels of the human breast for ever various, rolling without rest.
60.4: To every mortal is thy influence known, and men beneath thy righteous bondage groan;
60.5: For ev'ry thought within the mind conceal'd is to thy fight perspicuously reveal'd.
60.6: The soul unwilling reason to obey by lawless passion rul'd, thy eyes survey.
60.7: All to see, hear, and rule, O pow'r divine whose nature Equity contains, is thine.
60.8: Come, blessed, holy Goddess, hear my pray'r, and make thy mystic's life, thy constant care:
60.9: Give aid benignant in the needful hour, and strength abundant to the reas'ning pow'r;
60.10: And far avert the dire, unfriendly race of counsels impious, arrogant, and base.

61.2: The piercing eye of Justice [Dike] bright, I sing, plac'd by the throne of heav'n's almighty king [Zeus],
61.3: Perceiving thence, with vision unconfin'd, the life and conduct of the human kind
61.4: To thee, revenge and punishment belong, chastising ev'ry deed, unjust and wrong;
61.5: Whose pow'r alone, dissimilars can join, and from th' equality of truth combine:
61.6: For all the ill, persuasion can inspire, when urging bad designs, with counsel dire,
61.7: 'Tis thine alone to punish; with the race of lawless passions, and incentives base;
61.8: For thou art ever to the good inclin'd, and hostile to the men of evil mind.
61.9: Come, all-propitious, and thy suppliant hear, when Fate's predestin'd, final hour draws near.

62.2: O Blessed Equity [Dikaiosune], mankind's delight, th' eternal friend of conduct just and right:
62.3: Abundant, venerable, honor'd maid, to judgments pure, dispensing constant aid,
62.4: A stable conscience, and an upright mind; for men unjust, by thee are undermin'd,
62.5: Whose souls perverse thy bondage ne'er desire, but more untam'd decline thy scourges dire:
62.6: Harmonious, friendly power, averse to strife, in peace rejoicing, and a stable life;
62.7: Lovely, loquacious, of a gentle mind, hating excess, to equal deeds inclin'd:
62.8: Wisdom, and virtue of whate'er degree, receive their proper bound alone in thee.
62.9: Hear, Goddess Equity [Dikaiosune], the deeds destroy of evil men, which human life annoy;
62.10: That all may yield to thee of mortal birth, whether supported by the fruits of earth,
62.11: Or in her kindly fertile bosom found, or in the depths of Marine Jove [Zeus] profound.

63.1: The holy king of Gods and men I call, celestial Law [Nomos], the righteous seal of all;
63.2: The seal which stamps whate'er the earth contains, Nature's firm basis, and the liquid plains:
63.3: Stable, and starry, of harmonious frame, preserving laws eternally the same:
63.4: Thy all-composing pow'r in heaven appears, connects its frame, and props the starry spheres;
63.5: And shakes weak Envy with tremendous sound, toss'd by thy arm in giddy whirls around.
63.6: 'Tis thine, the life of mortals to defend, and crown existence with a blessed end;
63.7: For thy command and alone, of all that lives order and rule to ev'ry dwelling gives:
63.8: Ever observant of the upright mind, and of just actions the companion kind;
63.9: Foe to the lawless, with avenging ire, their steps involving in destruction dire.
63.10: Come, bless, abundant pow'r, whom all revere, by all desir'd, with favr'ing mind draw near;
63.11: Give me thro' life, on thee to fix my fight, and ne'er forsake the equal paths of right.

64.2: Magnanimous, unconquer'd, boistrous Mars, in darts rejoicing, and in bloody wars
64.3: Fierce and untam'd, whose mighty pow'r can make the strongest walls from their foundations shake:
64.4: Mortal destroying king, defil'd with gore, pleas'd with war's dreadful and tumultuous roar:
64.5: Thee, human blood, and swords, and spears delight, and the dire ruin of mad savage fight.
64.6: Stay, furious contests, and avenging strife, whose works with woe, embitter human life;
64.7: To lovely Venus [Kypris], and to Bacchus [Lyaios] yield, to Ceres [Deo] give the weapons of the field;
64.8: Encourage peace, to gentle works inclin'd, and give abundance, with benignant mind.

65.1: The Fumigation from Frankincense and Manna.
65.2: Strong, mighty Vulcan [Hephaistos], bearing splendid light, unweary'd fire, with flaming torrents bright:
65.3: Strong-handed, deathless, and of art divine, pure element, a portion of the world is thine:
65.4: All-taming artist, all-diffusive pow'r, 'tis thine supreme, all substance to devour:
65.5: Æther, Sun, Moon, and Stars, light pure and clear, for these thy lucid parts to men appear.
65.6: To thee, all dwellings, cities, tribes belong, diffus'd thro' mortal bodies bright and strong.
65.7: Hear, blessed power, to holy rites incline, and all propitious on the incense shine:
65.8: Suppress the rage of fires unweary'd frame, and still preserve our nature's vital flame.

66.2: Great Esculapius [Asklepios], skill'd to heal mankind, all-ruling Pæan, and physician kind;
66.3: Whose arts medic'nal, can alone assuage diseases dire, and stop their dreadful rage:
66.4: Strong lenient God, regard my suppliant pray'r, bring gentle Health, adorn'd with lovely hair;
66.5: Convey the means of mitigating pain, and raging, deadly pestilence restrain.
66.6: O pow'r all-flourishing, abundant, bright, Apollo's honor'd offspring, God of light;
66.7: Husband of blameless Health [Hygeia], the constant foe of dread Disease the minister of woe:
66.8: Come, blessed saviour, and my health defend, and to my life afford a prosp'rous end.

67.2: O Much-desir'd, prolific, gen'ral queen, hear me, life-bearing, Health [Hygeia], of beauteous mien,
67.3: Mother of all; by thee diseases dire, of bliss destructive, from our life retire;
67.4: And ev'ry house is flourishing and fair, if with rejoicing aspect thou art there:
67.5: Each dædal art, thy vig'rous force inspires, and all the world thy helping hand desires;
67.6: Pluto life's bane alone resists thy will, and ever hates thy all-preserving skill.
67.7: O fertile queen, from thee forever flows to mortal life from agony repose;
67.8: And men without thy all-sustaining ease, find nothing useful, nothing form'd to please;
67.9: Without thy aid, not Plutus' [Aides'] self can thrive, nor man to much afflicted age arrive;
67.10: For thou alone of countenance serene, dost govern all things, universal queen.
67.11: Assist thy mystics with propitious mind, and far avert disease of ev'ry kind.

68.2: Vociferous Bacchanalian Furies [Erinyes], hear! Ye, I invoke, dread pow'rs, whom all revere;
68.3: Nightly, profound, in secret who retire, Tisiphone, Alecto, and Megara dire:
68.4: Deep in a cavern merg'd, involv'd in night, near where Styx flows impervious to the sight;
68.5: Ever attendant on mysterious rites, furious and fierce, whom Fate's dread law delights;
68.6: Revenge and sorrows dire to you belong, hid in a savage veil, severe and strong,
68.7: Terrific virgins, who forever dwell endu'd with various forms, in deepest hell;
68.8: Aerial, and unseen by human kind, and swiftly coursing, rapid as the mind.
68.9: In vain the Sun with wing'd refulgence bright, in vain the Moon, far darting milder light,
68.10: Wisdom and Virtue may attempt in vain; and pleasing, Art, our transport to obtain
68.11: Unless with these you readily conspire, and far avert your all-destructive ire.
68.12: The boundless tribes of mortals you descry, and justly rule with Right's [Dike's] impartial eye.
68.13: Come, snaky-hair'd, Fates [Moirai] many-form'd, divine, suppress your rage, and to our rites incline.

69.2: Hear me, illustrious Furies [Eumenides], mighty nam'd, terrific pow'rs, for prudent counsel fam'd;
69.3: Holy and pure, from Jove terrestrial [Zeus Khthonios] born
69.4: and Proserpine [Phersephone], whom lovely locks adorn:
69.5: Whose piercing sight, with vision unconfin'd, surveys the deeds of all the impious kind:
69.6: On Fate attendant, punishing the race (with wrath severe) of deeds unjust and base.
69.7: Dark-colour'd queens, whose glittering eyes, are bright with dreadful, radiant, life-destroying, light:
69.8: Eternal rulers, terrible and strong, to whom revenge, and tortures dire belong;
69.9: Fatal and horrid to the human sight, with snaky tresses wand'ring in the night;
69.10: Either approach, and in these rites rejoice, for ye, I call, with holy, suppliant voice.
69.12: Call Melinoe, saffron-veil'd, terrene, who from infernal Pluto's sacred queen [Phersephone],
69.13: Mixt with Saturnian Jupiter [Kronion Zeus], arose, near where Cocytus' mournful river flows;
69.15: Jove [Zeus] divine deceiv'd with guileful arts dark Proserpine [Phersephone].
69.16: Hence, partly black thy limbs and partly white, from Pluto [Plouton] dark, from Jove [Zeus] etherial, bright
69.17: Thy colour'd members, men by night inspire when seen in specter'd forms with terrors dire;
69.18: Now darkly visible, involv'd in night, perspicuous now they meet the fearful fight.
69.19: Terrestrial queen expel wherever found the soul's mad fears to earth's remotest bound;
69.20: With holy aspect on our incense shrine, and bless thy mystics, and the rites divine.

71.2: Approach strong Fortune [Tykhe], with propitious mind and rich abundance, to my pray'r inclin'd
71.3: Placid, and gentle Trivia, mighty nam'd, imperial Dian [Artemis], born of Pluto [Eubouleos] fam'd;
71.4: Mankind's unconquer'd, endless praise is thine, sepulch'ral, widely-wand'ring pow'r divine!
71.5: In thee, our various mortal life is found, and some from thee hi copious wealth abound;
71.6: While others mourn thy hand averse to bless, in all the bitterness of deep distress.
71.7: Be present, Goddess, to thy vot'ry kind, and give abundance with benignant mind.

72.2: Thee, mighty-ruling, Dæmon dread, I call, mild Jove [Zeus], life-giving, and the source of all:
72.3: Great Jove [Zeus], much-wand'ring, terrible and strong, to whom revenge and tortures dire belong.
72.4: Mankind from thee, in plenteous wealth abound, when in their dwellings joyful thou art found;
72.5: Or pass thro' life afflicted and distress'd, the needful means of bliss by thee supprest.
72.6: 'Tis thine alone endu'd with boundless might, to keep the keys of sorrow and delight.
72.7: O holy, blessed father, hear my pray'r, disperse the seeds of life-consuming care;
72.8: With fav'ring mind the sacred rites attend, and grant my days a glorious, blessed end.

73.2: I Call Leucothea, of great Cadmus born, and Bacchus' [Dionysos'] nurse, whom ivy leaves adorn.
73.3: Hear, pow'rful Goddess, in the mighty deep wide and profound, thy Ration doom'd to keep:
73.4: In waves rejoicing, guardian of mankind; for ships from thee alone deliv'rance find
73.5: Amidst the fury of th' unstable main, when art no more avail, and strength is vain;
73.6: When rushing billows with tempestuous ire o'erwhelm the mariner in ruin dire,
73.7: Thou hear'st, with pity touch'd, his suppliant pray'r, resolv'd his life to succour and to spare.
73.8: Be ever present, Goddess! in distress, waft ships along with prosperous success:
73.9: Thy mystics thro' the stormy sea defend, and safe conduct them to their destin'd end.

74.2: O Nurs'd with Dionysius [Dionysos], doom'd to keep thy dwelling in the widely-spreading deep:
74.3: With joyful aspect to my pray'r incline, propitious come, and bless the rites divine:
74.4: Thro' earth and sea thy ministers attend, and from old Ocean's stormy waves defend:
74.5: For ships their safety ever owe to thee, who wand'rest with them thro' the raging sea.
74.6: Come, guardian pow'r, whom mortal tribes desire, and far avert the deep's destructive ire.

75.2: Daughters of Jove [Zeus and Mnemosyne], dire-sounding and divine,
75.4: To those whose breasts your sacred furies fire much-form'd, the objects of supreme desire:
75.5: Sources of blameless virtue to mankind, who form to excellence the youthful mind;
75.6: Who nurse the soul, and give her to descry the paths of right with Reason's steady eye.
75.7: Commanding queens who lead to sacred light the intellect refin'd from Error's night;
75.8: And to mankind each holy rite disclose, for mystic knowledge from your nature flows.
75.9: Clio, and Erato, who charms the sight, with thee Euterpe minist'ring delight:
75.10: Thalia flourishing, Polymina fam'd, Melpomene from skill in music nam'd:
75.11: Terpischore, Urania heav'nly bright, with thee who gav'st me to behold the light.
75.12: Come, venerable, various, pow'rs divine, with fav'ring aspect on your mystics shine;
75.13: Bring glorious, ardent, lovely, fam'd desire, and warm my bosom with your sacred fire.

76.2: The consort I invoke of Jove [Zeus] divine, source of the holy, sweetly-speaking Nine;
76.3: Free from th' oblivion of the fallen mind, by whom the soul with intellect is join'd:
76.4: Reason's increase, and thought to thee belong, all-powerful, pleasant, vigilant, and strong:
76.5: 'Tis thine, to waken from lethargic rest all thoughts deposited within the breast;
76.6: And nought neglecting, vigorous to excite the mental eye from dark oblivion's night.
76.7: Come, blessed power, thy mystic's mem'ry wake to holy rites, and Lethe's fetters break.

77.2: Hear me, O Goddess! whose emerging ray leads on the broad refulgence of the day;
77.3: Blushing Aurora [Eos], whose celestial light beams on the world with red'ning splendours bright:
77.4: Angel of Titan, whom with constant round, thy orient beams recall from night profound:
77.5: Labour of ev'ry kind to lead is thine, of mortal life the minister divine.
77.6: Mankind in thee eternally delight, and none presumes to shun thy beauteous sight.
77.7: Soon as thy splendours break the bands of rest, and eyes unclose with pleasing sleep oppress'd;
77.8: Men, reptiles, birds, and beasts, with gen'ral voice, and all the nations of the deep, rejoice;
77.9: For all the culture of our life is thine. Come, blessed pow'r! and to these rites incline:
77.10: Thy holy light increase, and unconfin'd diffuse its radiance on thy mystic's mind.

78.2: Illustrious Themis, of celestial birth, thee I invoke, young blossom of the earth;
78.3: Beauteous-eyed virgin; first from thee alone, prophetic oracles to men were known,
78.4: Giv'n from the deep recesses of the fane in sacred Pytho, where renown'd you reign;
78.5: From thee, Apollo's oracles arose, and from thy pow'r his inspiration flows.
78.6: Honour'd by all, of form divinely bright, majestic virgin, wand'ring in the night:
78.7: Mankind from thee first learnt initial rites, and Bacchus' nightly choirs thy soul delights;
78.8: For holy honours to disclose is thine, with all the culture of the pow'rs divine.
78.9: Be present, Goddess, to my pray'r inclin'd, and bless the mystic rites with fav'ring mind.

79.2: Boreas, whose wint'ry blasts, terrific, tear the bosom of the deep surrounding air;
79.3: Cold icy pow'r, approach, and fav'ring blow, and Thrace a while desert expos'd to snow:
79.4: The misty station of the air dissolve, with pregnant clouds, whose frames in show'rs resolve:
79.5: Serenely temper all within the sky, and wipe from moisture, Æther's beauteous eye.

80.2: Sea-born, aerial, blowing from the west, sweet gales [Aurai], who give to weary'd labour rest:
80.3: Vernal and grassy, and of gentle found, to ships delightful, thro' the sea profound;
80.4: For these, impell'd by you with gentle force, pursue with prosp'rous Fate their destin'd course.
80.5: With blameless gales regard my suppliant pray'r, Zephyrs unseen, light-wing'd, and form'd from air.

81.2: Wide coursing gales, whose lightly leaping feet with rapid wings the air's wet bosom beat,
81.3: Approach benevolent, swift-whirling pow'rs, with humid clouds the principles of flow'rs:
81.4: For flow'ry clouds are portion'd to your care, to send on earth from all surrounding air.
81.5: Bear, blessed pow'rs, these holy rites attend, and fruitful rains on earth all-parent send.

82.2: Ocean I call, whose nature ever flows, from whom at first both Gods and men arose;
82.3: Sire incorruptible, whose waves surround, and earth's concluding mighty circle bound:
82.4: Hence every river, hence the spreading sea, and earth's pure bubbling fountains spring from thee:
82.5: Hear, mighty fire, for boundless bliss is thine, whose waters purify the pow'rs divine:
82.6: Earth's friendly limit, fountain of the pole, whose waves wide spreading and circumfluent roll.
82.7: Approach benevolent, with placid mind, and be for ever to thy mystics kind.

83.2: Daughter of Saturn [Kronos], venerable dame, the seat containing of unweary'd flame;
83.3: In sacred rites these ministers are thine, Mystics much-blessed, holy and divine
83.4: In thee, the Gods have fix'd place, strong, stable, basis of the mortal race:
83.5: Eternal, much-form'd ever-florid queen, laughing and blessed, and of lovely mien;
83.6: Accept these rites, accord each just desire, and gentle health, and needful good inspire.

84.2: Sleep [Hypnos], king of Gods, and men of mortal birth, sov'reign of all sustain'd by mother Earth;
84.3: For thy dominion is supreme alone, o'er all extended, and by all things known.
84.4: 'Tis thine all bodies with benignant mind in other bands than those of brass to bind:
84.5: Tamer of cares, to weary toil repose, from whom sweet solace in affliction flows.
84.6: Thy pleasing, gentle chains preserve the soul, and e'en the dreadful cares of death controul;
84.7: For Death [Thanatos] and Lethe with oblivious stream, mankind thy genuine brothers justly deem.
84.8: With fav'ring aspect to my pray'r incline, and save thy mystics in their works divine.

85.2: Thee I invoke, blest pow'r of dreams [Oneiroi] divine, angel of future fates, swift wings are thine:
85.3: Great source of oracles to human kind, when stealing soft, and whisp'ring to the mind,
85.4: Thro' sleep's sweet silence and the gloom of night, thy pow'r awakes th' intellectual fight;
85.5: To silent souls the will of heav'n relates, and silently reveals their future fates.
85.6: For ever friendly to the upright mind sacred and pure, to holy rites inclin'd;
85.7: For these with pleasing hope thy dreams inspire, bliss to anticipate, which all desire.
85.8: Thy visions manifest of fate disclose, what methods best may mitigate our woes;
85.9: Reveal what rites the Gods immortal please, and what the means their anger to appease:
85.10: For ever tranquil is the good man's end, whose life, thy dreams admonish and defend.
85.11: But from the wicked turn'd averse to bless, thy form unseen, the angel of distress;
85.12: No means to cheek approaching ill they find, pensive with fears, and to the future blind.
85.13: Come, blessed pow'r, the signatures reveal which heav'n's decrees mysteriously conceal,
85.14: Signs only present to the worthy mind, nor omens ill disclose of monst'rous kind.

86.2: Hear me, O Death [Thanatos], whose empire unconfin'd, extends to mortal tribes of ev'ry kind.
86.3: On thee, the portion of our time depends, whose absence lengthens life, whose presence ends.
86.4: Thy sleep perpetual bursts the vivid folds, by which the soul, attracting body holds:
86.5: Common to all of ev'ry sex and age, for nought escapes thy all-destructive rage;
86.6: Not youth itself thy clemency can gain, vig'rous and strong, by thee untimely slain.
86.7: In thee, the end of nature's works is known, in thee, all judgment is absolv'd alone:
86.8: No suppliant arts thy dreadful rage controul, no vows revoke the purpose of thy soul;
86.9: O blessed pow'r regard my ardent pray'r, and human life to age abundant spare.
